- 2026-08-05T06:42:28.902Z — chose **D14, three parts (user request): (a) `sofar statusline --install` — a one-command project-level installer that merges ONLY the statusLine key into <root>/.claude/settings.json, no hooks and no .sofar/, reusing init's merge law (existing statusLine always wins) and reporting wired/already/kept; (b) the identity segments quote Claude Code's default palette — dir YELLOW, branch BLUE — via a new non-semantic `Style.blue` reserved for exactly this and documented as unusable for state; (c) the model label drops `context` from a parenthesised window size, so "Opus 5 (1M context)" renders "Opus 5 (1M)". On color: D6 established that the rent-meter REPLACES Claude's default line and must not cost the user what it replaced, and that argument covers appearance as much as content — a reproduction that recolors its source is not a reproduction. Calling blue a quotation rather than a meaning keeps D1 honest: the law binds color to meaning, and the one member that carries no meaning is marked as such instead of being given a fake one. Dropping `context` is the same word-over-glyph economy as D10/D11 — on a line that already reports ctx fill, the noun is the one part nobody has to read.
- 2026-08-05T07:34:34.082Z — chose **D15: (a) `sofar statusline --uninstall` — the inverse of --install, deleting the statusLine key so the host tool's own line returns, reporting removed/absent/foreign; (b) `--user` on both verbs, retargeting ~/.claude/settings.json (every project) instead of the repo's; (c) init's statusline hint is suppressed when the personal ~/.claude/settings.json already wires sofar's line. The theirs-wins law now runs in BOTH directions: --uninstall deletes only a byte-for-byte match of sofar's own entry, so it can only undo what sofar did. The settings file survives a removal that empties it to {}. --install with --uninstall is an error, not a precedence rule.** over Leaving revert to `sofar uninit` (repo-scoped only, so it can never reach the personal settings file, and far too heavy when the user installed nothing but a status line); documenting the hand-edit in the README instead of shipping a command; a --force that removes a foreign statusLine; deleting the settings file when the removal empties it; and letting the hint keep firing on the grounds that it only claims to describe project settings because D14 shipped a way to wire the line and no way to unwire it, which is not a neutral omission: it means the only documented exit is hand-editing JSON, and at the --user scope uninit cannot help at all. Symmetry is the fix. The hint change is a correctness bug caught by dogfooding — after wiring the personal settings, every fresh `sofar init` announced "statusline not wired" while sofar's line was visibly rendering, telling the user to fix something that was not broken. Making the probe injectable also closed a real non-hermeticity in the test suite: three init tests had been passing only because no developer had yet wired the line personally, and they failed the moment one did.
